title: Flow notify: a record-triggered flow's notification links nowhere unless the author adds the source pair
body:
epic:#26676#1 · zhuangjianguo · session_cdb7a717def74e719988f089fbaa18ff

From a real-user walkthrough of the development flow, filed on the maintainer's word: 「第一组：会卡住人或误导人，立卡」 (2026-11-04). Measured on `main` `987ff33b88` unless a line says otherwise. Test project scaffolded with `create-objectstack@18.3.0`.

## What a customer sees

A technician is assigned a ticket, gets the notification, clicks it, and lands on the notification list, not the ticket. The author wrote the obvious flow, `recipients`, `title` and `message`, and `os validate` passed.

## Measured

- Published 18.3.0: `sys_inbox_message.action_url` is `null`, and the click opens `sys_inbox_message?view=mine`. Adding `sourceObject` and `sourceId: { dialect: 'cel', source: 'record.id' }` gave `actionUrl: /asset_repair_ticket/ID`, and the click opened the record.
- `main`: `packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/notify-node.ts`, near line 976, builds `source` only from the explicit pair. It reads nothing from the trigger.

The seat itself omitted the pair on the first write, while authoring from the skill.

## Expected

In a flow with a record trigger, a notify node with no source and no `actionUrl` links to the triggering record. An explicit `actionUrl` or pair still wins. A flow with no trigger record stays as it is.
